sources.snippet: Results Generalization across benchmarks, model sizes, and answer agents Memory-R2 transfers to out-of-distribution benchmarks (LongMemEval-oracle/-s, MSC-Self-Instruct, MemBench), generalizes from 3B to 7B with the largest gains on the smaller model, and is robust across answer agents (base Qwen-7B, GRPO-tuned Qwen-7B, GPT-OSS-120B).

sources.snippet: Memory-augmented LLM agents enable interactions that extend beyond finite context windows by storing, updating, and reusing information across sessions. However, training such agents with reinforcement learning in multi-session environments is challenging because memory turns the agent's past actions into part of its future environment. sources.snippet: The trained memory policy also generalizes to different answer agents: fixing the answer module while varying the memory policy produces consistently strong scores. These results indicate the learned memory-construction policy is robust rather than overfit to benchmark-specific patterns or model sizes.
